newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia hails oil find, sees more exploration.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia hails oil find, sees more exploration.

text.p: An oil find in eastern Mongolia was a milestone for the nation's energy sector and will spur more foreign investment in exploration, a top Mongolian oil official said on Wednesday.
"It is extremely important for the country's economy," G. Enkhbold, chairman of the Petroleum Authority of Mongolia, told Reuters in an interview.
"Mongolia will make money out of this discovery."

SOCO International Plc announced this week its SOTAMO 19-3 well in the Tamsag basin flowed about 687 barrels of oil per day. The 37 API gravity oil flowed from intervals at depths ranging from 2,385 to 2,421 metres.
The Petroleum Authority of Mongolia has a production sharing agreement with SOCO.
Mongolian officials said the London-listed company has drilled six wells and four have found varying amounts of oil.
Oil resources had been exploited in the country in past years with the help of the former Soviet Union but those wells eventually were abandoned.

Mongolia has no data on proven oil resources but it has been eager to attract foreign energy companies to develop resources to give its ailing economy a boost and reduce its dependence on costly imported energy.
Last month, new regulations took effect, substantially improving terms for foreign investors in the oil sector by eliminating income tax that had reached 40 percent.
Mongolia requires production sharing but royalty payments have been made negotiable and do not exceed 10 percent.
"These changes are very good for our industry," said Enkhbold.
SOCO officials said they had invested $17 million to explore in four blocks covering 40,000 sq km in the Tamsag basin.
Nescor of the United States is also exploring for oil in southeast Mongolia and three Canadian companies are interested in other blocks, Enkhbold said without giving further details.

Most of the interest in oil exploration in Mongolia has been in these eastern or southeastern regions, where transport and exploration data are better. These areas are also closer to China, another potential market.
